top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn and Hanson, B022) rests on a first-order question: who bears the cost when trade and technology shocks change labour demand, and why adjustment in particular places is slow and costly. Its designs are transparent and have been replicated, re-analysed and contested for about a decade. The dispute concerns the size and persistence of the effects, not whether adjustment costs exist. Credit for the named evidence is clean, because the three are joint authors of the central China-shock papers. The citation should be limited to the empirical evidence on import competition, technological change, labour demand and local labour markets. It should not claim the task-model theory, whose originators (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane) are outside the credited set. The Scientific Background should address the persistence and shift-share critiques directly. P002 (Melitz and Helpman, B012) is a mature, well-confirmed and cleanly attributed two-name award with a stable core mechanism. I rank it second because its credit boundary is exposed to Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum, and its welfare magnitudes depend on functional form. The choice between P001 and P002 is a close weighting of conceptual foundation against evidence on distributional adjustment, not a clear gap in merit. Both are clearly preferable to no award (P000), which I rank last because both proposals name prize-level, adequately attributable discoveries.
recusal_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Melitz or Helpman is apparent from the profile. I disclose that my work is in the design-based empirical labour tradition closest to P001, and that my class-size paper (with Öckert and Oosterbeek) is cited in the 2021 Scientific Background. I chaired the Committee in 2019-21 and gave the 2021 presentation speech. My Stockholm University overlap with Hassler and Krusell was institutional, not co-authorship. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
